- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is low or volatile (e.g., post-80+ peaks, sentiment < 0.4).
- Underestimate sharp upward moves when sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat (e.g., sentiment > 0.6 but price stuck near 78–79).
- Lag in downward corrections: model often delays price drops, especially when sentiment is weak (e.g., sentiment < 0.3, price drops > 1.5% from peak).
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect after strong rallies, pushing prices back too aggressively (e.g., forecast 83+ after 82+ peak, then drops to 80+).
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops sharply, model should reduce forecast slope, not just reset.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is flat, model should not assume continuation; instead, expect mean reversion or consolidation.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model should not assume breakout — instead, treat as consolidation or delayed reaction.
